slides.title: Why your espresso tastes bitter
slides.subtitle: It's rarely the beans. Three causes, and the one fix to try first.

slides.title: Bitter means too much extracted
slides.body: Hot water pulls flavor out of coffee in stages. Fruity, sweet notes come first. Bitter, harsh ones come last. Bitter espresso is called over-extracted: the water took too much.
slides.highlight: Bitterness is a sign of going too far.

slides.title: The usual suspect: grind
slides.body: Finer grounds slow the water down. It stays in contact with the coffee longer and drags out the bitter parts. A shot that drips slowly is the classic sign.

slides.caption: A typical espresso shot time. Much longer, and bitterness often creeps in.

slides.label: The fix
slides.body: Grind one step coarser, pull a shot, taste. Change one thing at a time, then adjust again.

slides.title: Bitter? Go a little coarser
slides.body: Bitter means over-extracted. Coarser grind, shorter shot, taste, repeat.
slides.cta: Save it for your next shot
